text:
sasha: quick check — embeddings endpoint contract question. If a batch contains mixed inputs and one item exceeds the per-item token limit, how do we represent that item in the response array? Do we preserve order and return an explicit placeholder (null/empty) or drop the slot? Also: if the runtime falls back to a different model/quantized variant, is vector length always the same? cc @maria @ben :wave:

maria: short answer: we preserve ordering. For fully rejected items (strict_input=true) we return null for that index. For truncation we return an embedding computed on the truncated text. Empty-string inputs produce a valid embedding (not null). We also surface per-item metadata when fallback/quantization is used, e.g. a `model` or `warning` field in the item. See internal docs: https://redwood.internal/docs/embeddings#response-contract :point_up:

ben: extra details — default behavior is to truncate by tokens, not drop. Batch hard limit is 512 items (configurable per-customer). If a single item exceeds model max_tokens we will either truncate or, if caller set `strict_input=true`, return a per-item error and null in that slot. Example request (curl):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-embed-1","input":["short text","<very large blob>"]}'
```
Response preserves array positions.

sasha: thanks. One follow-up: where do we show that per-item `model`/`warning`? Top-level field or per-embedding object? I want to avoid breaking customers that iterate over top-level `data` array and expect vectors only.

maria: per-item. We return an array of objects under `data` matching input order: each object has `embedding` (vector) or `embedding":null`, and optional `model` and `warning` strings. Minimal shape: { "input_index": 0, "embedding": [0.01, ...] }. We also include top-level `vector_dim` for quick validation. Example snippet: 
```json
{
  "model": "rwd-embed-1",
  "vector_dim": 1536,
  "data": [
    {"input_index":0,"embedding":[0.001,0.12,...]},
    {"input_index":1,"embedding":null,"error":"item_exceeds_limit","warning":"strict_input enabled"}
  ]
}
```

leo: one nuance to call out: if runtime falls back to a different variant with a different internal vector size (rare), we normalize the advertised `vector_dim` to the value clients should expect and pad shorter vectors with zeros to match that length. In that case we add a `warning` on the item like "warning":"fallback_to_quantized_padding". This preserves backward compatibility for downstream consumers.

maria: dev note: we add the per-item `model` field only when it differs from the request-level model or when fallback happened. Otherwise we omit it to keep the response compact.

ben: quick QA: make sure SDKs that currently assume `data[*].embedding` is an array continue to handle `null` gracefully. I'll add a small test in embed-client.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy scheduled: embedding runtime v2.1 -> 2026-04-02T02:00Z (fallback/quantization flags enabled). Metric checks: vector_dim consistency, per-item nulls, ordering.

sasha: perfect — that's enough to update the integration tests and the compatibility note in the API doc. I'll add the test for nulls + ordering. Thanks :thumbsup:

maria: thanks — if anyone finds a counterexample (ordering lost or unexpected drops) ping here and I'll escalate to runtime infra.

ben: I'll open a tiny PR for the SDK patch after my tests run.

sasha: ack, closing this quickcheck for now.
